author: claude-prob1000-F-0908
key_identity: theta(p_c) > 0 and Thm 1.2 => liminf = 0; Conj 1.4 => liminf > 0; contradiction
method: Split the conjecture by p. For p > p_c the supercritical finite-cluster tail is stretched exponential with exponent (d-1)/d (Kesten and Zhang 1990 for bond percolation, Grimmett's book Theorem 8.65; the site version follows the same Grimmett-Marstrand renormalisation), so the liminf is at least (d-1)/d > 0 and the conjecture holds there. The only case left is p = p_c with theta(p_c) > 0.
obstruction: Nothing beyond theta(p_c) = 0 itself; the reformulation does not suggest a new route because Theorem 1.2 already consumes the tail information at p_c.
result: Conjecture 1.4 is EQUIVALENT to Conjecture 1.1 (theta(p_c, Z^d) = 0) modulo the supercritical tail theorem: 1.4 at p = p_c together with the source's Theorem 1.2 gives theta(p_c) = 0 (if theta(p_c) > 0 then 1.4 makes the liminf positive while 1.2 makes it zero); conversely if theta(p_c) = 0 the p = p_c case of 1.4 is vacuous and the p > p_c case is Kesten-Zhang. So the row is a reformulation of C0023 rather than a new target, and its only content beyond theta(p_c) = 0 is the site-percolation version of the supercritical tail bound.

author: claude-prob1000-F-0908
method: Compare with the first-order analogue: for increasing A at p = 1/2, E|P^+_1(A)| = sum_i Inf_i(1_A) = 2 E[1_A (sum_i (2 omega_i - 1))] (monotone functions), which is maximised exactly by the majority set, i.e. the first-order maximiser IS a Hamming ball. Conjecture 53.1 asks the second-order functional to be maximised within two Hamming levels of majority.
obstruction: Exact form of phi_2 (formula (52.1), a 708-page source) not extracted in this session; the magnitude check above disagrees with the quoted bound and must be settled first.
result: The first-order statement is a two-line theorem; the second-order one has no such linear representation because a pivot of order two is a pair (i,j) with omega + e_i + e_j in A but neither single flip in A, a quadratic functional of 1_A. Sanity check: for A = majority with n odd, the second-order pivots at omega with sum = (n-3)/2 are all pairs of zero coordinates, of order n^2/4 per such omega, and the level has weight of order n^{-1/2}, giving phi_2/2^n of order n^{3/2}, not sqrt(n); so the bound E|P^+_2| <= 6 sqrt n quoted in the source must be read with the source's own normalisation of P^+_2 (which I did not verify in Section 51), and the row should be re-read against formulas (51.1)-(52.1) before any attack.

author: claude-prob1000-F-0908
method: Test the extreme cases. |B| = 1: {o <-> b} and E_b are both increasing, so Harris-FKG gives P[{o<->b} cap E_b] >= P[o<->b] P[E_b] >= (1-eps) P[o<->b], i.e. phi(eps) = 1 - eps works. General B: for the family of graphs where the connections o <-> b, b in B, are independent (disjoint routes) with common probability q, take the adversarial choice E_b = {o <-> B \ {b}}; then P[E_b] >= 1 - eps forces (1-q)^{|B|-1} <= eps and the union event is {N >= 2} with N ~ Binomial(|B|, q), whose failure P[N = 1] = |B| q (1-q)^{|B|-1} <= |B| q eps is at most eps log(1/eps) (1+o(1)) times P[N >= 1]; so on that family phi(eps) = 1 - O(eps log(1/eps)) works for this E_b.
obstruction: A counterexample needs 'o connects to exactly one boundary point with high probability, uniformly over many candidates'; positive association of the connection events works against such concentration, and I could not build a Bernoulli example with P[N = 1 | N >= 1] -> 1 while every P[o <-> B \ b] -> 1.
result: Two supporting cases, no proof and no counterexample. The conjecture is strictly stronger than Kozma-Nitzan's Conjecture 3 (the source proves the implication), so it is at least as hard as that.

author: claude-prob1000-F-0908
key_identity: P[o<->z] >= 1 - delta - delta E[N_A] (FKG on increasing x decreasing)
method: Union bound with FKG. P[o <-> z] >= P[o <-> A] - P[exists a in A: o <-> a, a not<-> z]. For fixed a the event {o <-> a} is increasing and {a not<-> z} is decreasing, so P[o<->a, a not<->z] <= P[o<->a] P[a not<->z] <= delta P[o<->a]. Summing, P[o <-> z] >= 1 - delta - delta E[N_A], where N_A is the number of a in A joined to o.
obstruction: No control of N_A in the interesting instances (boxes in Z^d with A a face: N_A is of order n^{d-1} there).
result: The conjecture holds with eta = 2 delta (K + 1) on every instance where E[N_A] <= K: in particular whenever |A| is bounded, and more generally whenever the cluster of o meets A in a bounded expected number of points. The open content is exactly the regime where o's cluster meets A in many points, where the union bound over a is wasteful; what is needed is that the cluster of o, given it reaches A, reaches A at some point a whose own event {a <-> z} occurs, i.e. an FKG-type statement conditional on the cluster, which is Flammant's Conjecture 2.2 with E_a = {a <-> z}.

author: claude-prob1000-F-0908
method: Read the tree proof for what breaks on Z^d: the source dominates nu_lambda from below by a product Bernoulli measure with parameter p_lambda and uses p_lambda < 1/(d-1) (the tree's site-percolation threshold) for lambda slightly above lambda_1; on the tree the branches below a vertex are conditionally independent, so a one-vertex density bound converts into a product-measure comparison. On Z^d there is no such conditional independence and the density of nu_lambda near lambda_1 is small (it vanishes continuously at lambda_c, Bezuidenhout-Grimmett), so the natural route is instead: show nu_lambda is dominated by a product measure of small density near lambda_c (which would give lambda_p > lambda_1 via p_c(Z^d) > 0).
obstruction: nu_lambda has no known finite-range decoupling; its correlations near lambda_c are exactly the hard part.
result: No result; the sharper formulation is: does the upper invariant measure at lambda_c + eps stochastically dominate no product measure of density above p_c^site(Z^d)? A positive answer for small eps gives the conjecture, since 'dominated by' is the wrong direction for percolation but 'density of infected sites tends to 0 as lambda -> lambda_c' (continuity of the transition) plus a finite-range decoupling of nu_lambda would give non-percolation for lambda near lambda_c.

author: claude-prob1000-F-0908
method: Reduce to a percolation-in-random-environment statement: nu_lambda is a translation-invariant (in the tree's automorphism group) measure with positive association (it is the limit of an attractive spin system started from all-infected, so it satisfies FKG, Harris 1977). For FKG measures on trees, continuity of the percolation function at the threshold is not automatic; the standard route (Bezuidenhout-Grimmett style finite-size criterion) needs a finite-range or exponentially decaying dependence, and nu_lambda on the tree is a Markov chain along rays only in the Boltzmann sense, not a genuine finite-range field.
obstruction: Decay of correlations of the upper invariant measure on T_d is not in the source and I did not find it elsewhere in the session.
result: No result. First concrete sub-question: does nu_lambda have exponential decay of correlations along the tree at every lambda > lambda_1? If so, a Grimmett-Marstrand type argument in the tree setting would give continuity of the infected-percolation function at lambda_p.

author: claude-prob1000-F-0908
corrected_by: G0008-A002 (same day): the 'all n for small p' claim is withdrawn; only the large-n Ornstein-Zernike statement stands.
method: Check the trivial regimes. p small: P_p(0 <-> (0,n)) = p^n (1 + O(p)) with the correction from the number of self-avoiding paths of length n + 2k, so monotonicity holds for p below some p_0 by the connective-constant bound (number of paths of length m between the points is at most mu^m and the ratio of consecutive terms is p mu (1+o(1)) < 1). p close to 1: P_p(0 <-> (0,n)) = theta(p)^2 + (finite-cluster term) where the second term decays exponentially in n with a monotone leading behaviour; monotonicity for large n follows from the Ornstein-Zernike asymptotics of the truncated two-point function (Campanino-Ioffe-Velenik), which give C n^{-1/2} e^{-n/xi} (1 + o(1)) along an axis, so P is eventually decreasing for every p != p_c.
obstruction: No mechanism at p = p_c; at other p, uniformity of the Ornstein-Zernike error terms in n from n = 1 is not available.
result: Partial: monotonicity holds for all n when p is small, and for all n >= n_0(p) when p != p_c (Ornstein-Zernike axis asymptotics at p < p_c, and at p > p_c via the truncated function). The open content is (i) all n at intermediate p, where exact enumeration to moderate n is the natural test, and (ii) p = p_c, where the two-point function decays as n^{-1/4+o(1)} on the triangular lattice and no monotonicity mechanism is known.

author: claude-prob1000-F-0908
method: Identify the obvious sufficient condition and the obvious obstruction. Sufficient: lambda(G) attained by a 'spread' Perron vector, e.g. the vector v with v^T A v = lambda |v|^2 having ||v||_infinity^2 <= C |v|^2 / |G| (delocalised Perron eigenvector); then the expected number of vertices in large components is controlled by the same second-moment computation that gives the source's maximum-degree-size components, and a sprinkling argument of Krivelevich-Sudakov type should give Omega(|G|). Obstruction: a clique of size s attached to a path of length |G| - s has lambda ~ s and p = 2/s gives components of size O(s), so no condition weaker than 'the Perron mass is not concentrated on o(|G|) vertices' can suffice.
obstruction: The sprinkling step needs expansion between the many maximum-degree-size components, which delocalisation alone does not give (a disjoint union of many small dense pieces has a delocalised Perron vector and no giant). So the correct condition must also bound the number of components at scale Delta, i.e. involve the second eigenvalue.
result: A candidate answer: delocalisation of the Perron eigenvector (||v||_infinity^2 <= C |v|_2^2/|G|) is necessary up to constants and plausibly sufficient; not proved.

author: claude-prob1000-F-0908
method: Interpolate the two known ends. Regular: largest component O(log|G|) (branching-process comparison with mean p Delta < 1). Complete bipartite K_{s,t}, t >> s: components of size about s log s at p = (1-eps)/sqrt(st). A natural guess is that the answer is governed by the largest eigenvalue of the 'non-backtracking' or 'square-root-degree-normalised' matrix restricted to a subgraph: the size of the largest component is max over induced subgraphs H of (log|H|) / log(1/(p lambda(H))) up to constants, i.e. the subgraph that is closest to critical dominates.
obstruction: The multiplicity term (how many near-critical subgraphs there are) is what the source's log|G| factor hides; no clean formulation reached.
result: A conjectural answer, no proof: largest component of order max_H log|H| / log(1/(p lambda(H))) with H ranging over induced subgraphs (for the regular graph H = G gives log|G|; for K_{s,t} the star K_{1,t} gives the t vertices of a star at p ~ 1/sqrt(st), consistent with the s log s scale only after the union over s stars, so the guess needs a multiplicity term).

author: claude-prob1000-F-0908
method: Reduce to a minimum-degree statement by the standard subgraph lemma: a graph of average degree d contains a subgraph of minimum degree at least d/2 (delete vertices of degree < d/2 one at a time). On that subgraph H, p >= (1+eps)/d = (1+eps)/(2 delta(H)) is only half-critical for H's minimum degree, so the reduction loses the factor 2 that makes the problem hard: the cycle must come from the sparse-but-dense-on-average structure, not from a min-degree core. Second reduction: by the source's own theorem, p >= (1+eps)/lambda(G) already gives a component of size Omega(Delta) at least; since lambda(G) >= d (average degree), p >= (1+eps)/d is supercritical for the spectral threshold, so a large component of size at least the maximum degree exists; the gap is turning a large component into a long cycle, which for regular graphs is the Krivelevich-Samotij DFS argument.
obstruction: The DFS/rotation-extension arguments need a degree lower bound on the explored subgraph; average degree gives none after the first deletions.
result: Two reductions and no proof; the second identifies the exact missing step (large component => long cycle without regularity).

author: claude-prob1000-F-0908
method: Look for the degree-inhomogeneous obstruction to the source's method. Its proof samples a 'plan' (a successor edge for every edge) and shows a simple plan has many deviations that must self-intersect, by an excursion reversal that is measure-preserving for the uniform non-backtracking step in a regular graph. With variable degrees the reversal changes the walk's law by the ratio of degrees along the excursion, which is the only place regularity enters; bounded degree ratio (max degree / min degree <= K) should therefore give the conjecture with C depending on K by the same proof.
obstruction: For a star-like hub of degree n the walk returns to the hub only if it re-enters through a neighbour, so hubs can make simple walks LONGER; a quantitative birthday bound in the hub regime is the open part.
result: Plausible extension to bounded degree ratio (not carried out); the genuine content of the conjecture is unbounded degrees (e.g. a few hubs of degree ~ n attached to a cubic graph), where a walk that hits a hub is sent to a uniformly random neighbour and the sqrt n scale competes with hub revisits.

author: claude-prob1000-F-0908
method: Write the objective as a maximisation of a supremum over transport plans: W_2^2(pi, lambda(x)lambda) = int |x|^2 dpi + int |y|^2 d(lambda(x)lambda) - 2 sup_{T in Pi(pi, lambda(x)lambda)} int <x,y> dT, and the first two terms are constant over Pi(lambda,lambda) (marginals fixed). So the conjecture says the diagonal coupling MINIMISES the maximal correlation sup_T int <x,y> dT with the product measure, over couplings of two uniforms. For the diagonal coupling this maximal correlation is that of the uniform law on the diagonal segment against the uniform law on the square, which is computable (the optimal map projects the square onto the diagonal monotonically along the direction (1,1)): value 1/2 + 1/12 ... (not computed to the end in this session).
obstruction: The Gaussian argument's key step (a Gaussian isoperimetric bound for the correlation functional) has no obvious uniform analogue with the right extremal set; not attempted further.
result: A reformulation only: the conjecture is a MINIMISATION of the maximal correlation with the product law over bivariate copulas. The Gaussian proof uses that the extremal set is determined by an isoperimetric inequality; the analogous tool for the square is the (known) isoperimetric profile of the cube, which suggests the same proof scheme could go through for the uniform law, with the diagonal replacing the Gaussian half-space extremals.

author: claude-prob1000-F-0908
method: Check the source's own reduction. Uniform integrability of the derivative martingale of a branching random walk holds if and only if the offspring point process satisfies the x log^2 x condition (Biggins-Kyprianou, Aidekon; Chen 2015 for the 'if and only if'), under the boundary case normalisation. So the conjecture's first half is a theorem the moment the cascade's offspring point process is shown to have E[X log_+^2 X] < infinity with X = sum over children of e^{theta* displacement}; the source's 'exponential-moment hypothesis on the offspring count' gives this directly when the displacements are bounded (then X <= N e^{theta* M} and E N log^2 N < infinity follows from the exponential moment).
obstruction: I did not read Theorem 2.1's hypotheses to confirm whether displacements are bounded; the row's status depends on that one check.
result: Under bounded displacements the first half (uniform integrability) follows from known results plus the source's exponential-moment hypothesis; the second half (Bramson delay and the decorated Gumbel limit) then needs the Aidekon / Madaule programme for branching random walks with the cascade's spine structure, which the source says is available from its [1, App. A]. If the displacements are unbounded the x log^2 x condition needs a separate tail estimate.

author: claude-prob1000-F-0908
method: Route around Miermont. For multitype Galton-Watson trees with a general (Polish) type space and a spectral gap for the mean-offspring kernel, the CRT limit can be obtained from the Lukasiewicz-path / height-process route of the single-type theory by projecting types away: the total-progeny walk is a Markov additive process with finite variance under the spectral-gap assumption, and de Raphelis (2017, 'Scaling limit of multitype Galton-Watson trees with infinitely many types') already handles infinitely many types under a spectral-gap/moment condition, giving the CRT with an explicit constant; the conjecture's constant Sigma_c should match his.
obstruction: de Raphelis's conditions (a Doeblin-type condition on the type kernel and moment bounds) must be checked against K; the 'D x R' type space with a diffusion coordinate may fail the Doeblin condition.
result: A literature route (de Raphelis 2017) that appears to cover the conjecture's setting, which would make the conjecture a corollary once the cascade cluster is written as a multitype Galton-Watson tree with the source's kernel K. Not verified against the source's exact hypotheses in this session.

author: claude-prob1000-0910
obstruction: As in A001, minus the withdrawn claim.
result: CORRECTION. The small-p claim of A001 ('monotonicity holds for all n when p is below some p_0') is withdrawn: the crude bounds p^n <= P_p(0 <-> (0,n)) <= sum_{k>=n} mu^k p^k give P_p(0<->(0,n+1)) <= (mu p)^{n+1}/(1 - mu p), which is NOT below p^n once mu^{n+1} p > 1 - mu p, i.e. for all large n at any fixed p (mu = 2.64.. is the connective constant); the low-order expansion P = p^n (1 + a_n p^2 + ...) has coefficients a_n growing with n, so uniformity in n is exactly what is missing. What stands: for every fixed p < p_c, P_p(0 <-> x) = C(p, x/|x|) |x|^{-1/2} e^{-|x|/xi_p(x/|x|)} (1 + o(1)) (Campanino-Ioffe 2002, Ornstein-Zernike for Bernoulli percolation), so the axis two-point function is eventually decreasing; for p > p_c the same holds for the truncated function in d = 2 (Campanino-Ioffe-Louidor 2010). So the partial result is: eventual monotonicity at every p != p_c; nothing at p_c; nothing for small n.

author: claude-prob1000-0910
key_identity: W_2^2(., nu) convex => max over Pi(lambda,lambda) at an extreme point; Birkhoff in the discrete case
method: (1) Convexity: pi -> W_2^2(pi, lambda (x) lambda) is convex and weakly continuous on the convex weakly compact set Pi(lambda, lambda), so by Bauer's maximum principle the supremum is attained at an EXTREME doubly stochastic measure. Deterministic couplings (id, T)_# lambda with T measure-preserving are extreme, but for nonatomic marginals not every extreme point is of that form (Lindenstrauss 1965, Losert's example), so this reduces the conjecture to extreme couplings, not all the way to maps. (2) Discretisation: marginals uniform on n equally spaced atoms, couplings = doubly stochastic matrices / n; there every extreme point IS a permutation (Birkhoff), so the discrete conjecture is 'the identity and the reversal maximise W_2^2(pi_sigma, U_n (x) U_n) over permutations sigma', with each value a transportation LP (n^2 grid points to n atoms). Exhaustive search (prob1000_lean_20260908/g0013_permutation_search.py, scipy HiGHS).
obstruction: The continuous statement needs either (a) the extreme-point reduction pushed to maps, or (b) a direct proof for the discrete permutation problem uniform in n plus a Gamma-convergence/approximation step. For (b), the runner-up pattern suggests an exchange argument: uncrossing two atoms of a non-monotone permutation should increase the transport cost to the product law; not proved.
result: MEASURED (exact LP values): for n = 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 (6, 24, 120, 720, 5040 permutations) the maximum is attained EXACTLY by the identity and the reversal and by nothing else; maxima 0.098765, 0.109375, 0.102400, 0.103395, 0.101624; runner-ups are the identity or reversal with one adjacent transposition at an end (e.g. n=7: 0.096626 vs 0.101624). The discrete conjecture holds for n <= 7. The values hover near 0.10; for the continuous diagonal coupling the analogous quantity should be the limit.

author: claude-prob1000-0910
cross_ledger: Codex tree Downloads/Probability_1000_20h_20260906 (row P0291, Leskela 2022 Problem 3 journal / Problem 2 arXiv)
key_identity: F(g) = C + alpha e^{-bg} + beta e^{-(2a+b)g}; b alpha + (2a+b) beta = b pi_2 [2Phi11 + Phi22 + Phi33 - Phi12 - Phi13 - Phi21 - Phi31]; S(psi) = sum of 11 weighted elementary supermodular inequalities.
method: Candidate: symmetric 3-state star (1->2 and 1->3 at rate a, 2->1 and 3->1 at rate b); not monotone since P_t(1,{3}) = at + O(t^2) > P_t(2,{3}) = O(t^2). Proof of the supermodular time ordering (2): reduce to monotonicity in each gap; for a reversible 3-state chain E phi as a function of one gap is C + alpha e^{-bg} + beta e^{-(2a+b)g}, so gap-monotonicity <=> (C1) Phi22+Phi33 >= Phi23+Phi32 and (C2) 2Phi11+Phi22+Phi33 >= Phi12+Phi13+Phi21+Phi31 for the two-point conditional Phi; leaf labels are exchangeable fair coins per excursion; (C1) by block comonotonicity; (C2) via the order-preserving coupling of the centre-started and leaf-started skeletons (fair coin on the overlap excursion) reduces to S(psi) >= 0 for supermodular psi on {1,2,3}^4, which is an exact nonnegative combination of 11 elementary increasing-difference inequalities (rational-verified).
obstruction: None mathematical. Owed: independent referee of the spectral step and of the coupling's marginal correctness; citation search on Leskela 2022 / Bauerle-Rolski 1998 for a prior 3-state example; the Codex ledger row should be updated by its owner.
result: YES: a stationary ergodic CTMC on three ordered values that is not stochastically monotone but satisfies c1 <= c2 => lambda_{c1} >=_sm lambda_{c2}, for every a, b > 0 (and by Bauerle-Rolski a non-monotone environment obeying Ross's monotonicity (1)). Smallest possible state space (two-state chains are monotone). Controls: exact LP dual test of >=_sm on {1,2,3}^n passes for n = 3,4,5 and rate pairs (1,1),(1,3),(3,1),(1,4); the clockwise 3-cycle control fails; the birth-death control passes; (C1),(C2) computed directly from conditional expectations have minima 0 to 1e-15. Boundary (measured): the asymmetric star with return rates b2 < b3 fails (2); b2 > b3 and a2 != a3 pass.

author: claude-prob1000-0910
cross_ledger: Codex tree Downloads/Probability_1000_20h_20260906 (row P0292, Leskela 2022 Problem 4 journal / Problem 3 arXiv)
key_identity: slow-mode coefficient of P_s(1,3) is c1 = pi3 b3 v1(1)^2 / ((b3 - mu1) <v1,v1>_pi), with min(b2,b3) < mu1 < max(b2,b3) strictly when b2 != b3; bivariate condition for ANY reversible 3-state chain: l1(1) l1(3) <= 0 for the slow left eigenvector l1 = pi v1.
method: Restrict to the star family on 1<2<3 (1->2 at a2, 1->3 at a3, 2->1 at b2, 3->1 at b3; always reversible, never monotone). Spectral one-gap reduction of the P0291 memo. Necessity from the two-point (concordance) condition via Cauchy interlacing of the arrowhead generator; sufficiency for b2 = b3 via the biased-coin version of the block certificate (S_p = sum_k p^k q^{3-k} T_k, each T_k an exact certificate).
obstruction: For b2 > b3 the leaf-period length depends on the label, so the centre/leaf skeleton is not an autonomous Markov chain and the finite block reduction does not apply; a proof needs either a new coupling of the three prefix laws or a different route to the two spectral inequalities.
result: PARTIAL, on the star family: (2) FAILS whenever b3 > b2 (already for n = 2: P_s(1,3) overshoots, so P(X_0<=1, X_s<=2) eventually increases) and HOLDS whenever b2 = b3, for all arrival rates a2, a3 > 0 (Theorem 2 of the memo). Conjecture: on stars (2) <=> b2 >= b3; the b2 > b3 case passed the exact LP dual test of >=_sm at n = 3, 4 at every point tried (p0292_star_family_map.out) but is unproved. So the characterisation Leskela asks for is neither monotonicity nor symmetry; on three states the two-point condition is the sign condition l1(1) l1(3) <= 0 on the slow left eigenvector, and whether it is also sufficient beyond stars is being mapped on random reversible 3-state chains (p0292_random_3state_map.py).

author: claude-prob1000-0910
cross_ledger: Codex tree Downloads/Probability_1000_20h_20260906 (row P0290, Leskela 2022 Problem 2 journal / Problem 1-related arXiv)
key_identity: J_f(c) = sum_l A_l h(lambda_l c), h(z) = (e^z - 1 - z)/z^2, A_l = ((pi f)^T V)_l (V^{-1} f)_l; E[workload] = E[N] for exponential unit service; R solves A0 + R A1 + R^2 A2 = 0.
method: Two instruments. (i) Light traffic: by the campaign's uniform expansion (P0289 proof file) w(c) = eps a/2 + eps^2 J_f(c) + O(eps^3) with J_f(c) = int_0^1 (1-u) E[f(X_0) f(X_{cu})] du, so (1) fails for small eps iff J_f rises somewhere; J_f computed exactly from the eigendecomposition and, where ill-conditioned, by expm quadrature. The earlier attempt P0290-A001 only used reversible X, where every autocovariance is a nonnegative mixture of decaying exponentials and J_f is automatically monotone; doubly monotone chains need not be reversible (explicit 3-state example with a circulation: rates 1.2, 0.1 / 0.8, 1.2 / 0.5, 0.8), and 4-state doubly monotone chains with complex eigenvalues exist (7 of 40 sampled). (ii) Moderate load: exact mean workload of the MMPP/M/1 queue by the matrix-geometric QBD solution, scanned in c at loads 0.2-0.85 (p0290_qbd_workload.py).
obstruction: If Problem 2 is true it needs a proof that goes beyond the supermodular order (which f(X) violates); the light-traffic coefficient's monotonicity for all f on doubly monotone chains is itself an unproved empirical regularity here (R_f can rise but J_f did not in any case tried). If it is false, the counterexample is not at light traffic and not among small random doubly monotone chains at moderate load; a targeted construction (large circulation, service distribution other than exponential/deterministic) is the next thing to try.
result: NEGATIVE SEARCH, no counterexample: on 140 random doubly monotone non-reversible generators (3, 4, 5 states) times every Boolean f and 30 random nonnegative f, and in a 20-restart hill-climb inside the doubly monotone cone, J_f never rises (the one apparent rise was an eigen-decomposition artefact at eigenvalues -221/-64 and disappears under direct quadrature: J = 0.49932, 0.49928, 0.49924, 0.49920, 0.49915 at c = 10, 30, 49, 68, 90). The AUTOCOVARIANCE itself can rise: a 4-state doubly monotone chain with f = 1_{2,3} has E f(X_0) f(X_t) = 0.060015 at t = 0.90 and 0.061145 at t = 10 (expm-verified), so the Codex observation that f(X) can violate (2) extends to a non-monotone autocovariance, yet the (1-u)-weighted second-order workload coefficient stays monotone. Exact QBD workload on the 3-state hand example is monotone in c for five Boolean f at loads 0.2, 0.5, 0.8; the random-chain QBD scan found no rise in the part completed before its time limit (a smaller rerun is in p0290_qbd_random.out). Contrast: the star chains of P0291 show that NON-monotone intensities can satisfy (1); Problem 2 asks the converse direction (monotone hidden chain, non-monotone image).
